body:
In the simplest case, you should be able to tell angular explicitly what the expected content type is, by passing it in to the request : `http.get(url, { contentType: 'string' })` 

For more complex cases, you can implement an interceptor that could handle this for you. 

If a responseType isn't passed, we default to JSON (because that's what 99% of cases are) - which is probably what's tripping you up. I believe this is the intended behavior cc @alxhub

Yes @robwormald I understand that the default response type is JSON, but it has been for a long time, and I banked on it. Only it used to not throw this parse exception and now it does. So it's not because I am making an assumption I don't understand, it's the assumption I have always made and it has been fine until this release.

I also don't see what good could possibly come from trying to parse an empty string **knowing** you will get an exception. Why not say undefined or null.  I guess undefined makes better sense since "null" parses to null.

@robwormald As far as i can see it's not possible to set contentType/responseType, as the typings declaration says it has to be a value of 'json' or undefined.

Typescript error message:
```
ERROR in E:/development/goprojects/src/github.com/zlepper/physicalStore/frontend/src/app/services/lists.service.ts (33,83): Argument of type '{ headers: HttpHeaders; responseType: "string"; }' is not assignable to parameter of type '{ headers?: HttpHeaders | undefined; observe?: "body" | undefined; params?: HttpParams | undefine...'.
  Type '{ headers: HttpHeaders; responseType: "string"; }' is not assignable to type '{ headers?: HttpHeaders | undefined; observe?: "body" | undefined; params?: HttpParams | undefine...'.
    Types of property 'responseType' are incompatible.
      Type '"string"' is not assignable to type '"json" | undefined'.

```

issue.title: HttpClient fails to parse an empty 200 response in IE11

## Current behavior The [HttpClient](https://angular.io/api/common/http/HttpClient) throws an error "_Http failure during parsing for ..._" in the case of an empty 200 response in IE11. The issue is not reproducible in Chrome and Firefox. Setting a _responseType_ option to "_text_" helps to resolve the issue. ## Expected behavior IE11 returns null by analogue with other browsers. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions Make an [HttpClient.get](https://angular.io/api/common/http/HttpClient#get) request to an endpoint with the an empty file in IE11. See this [plunker](http://plnkr.co/edit/6CVGCdVdr2ggxcVVnnD1?p=preview) for an example. ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? It is expected to have a consistent behavior across all browsers. ## Environment Angular version: 4.3.4 Browser: - [ ] Chrome (desktop) version XX - [ ] Chrome (Android) version XX - [ ] Chrome (iOS) version XX - [ ] Firefox version XX - [ ] Safari (desktop) version XX - [ ] Safari (iOS) version XX - [x] IE version 11 - [ ] Edge version XX For Tooling issues: - Node version: 6.10 - Platform: Windows

body:
`responseType: "text"` is the incantation you're looking for.

Yes, you will get an error if your server does not respond with valid JSON, unless you specifically tell Angular not to expect JSON.

But null, since there isn't a standard way to represent it, I guess gets translated across the wire as an empty string. My API is returning null which gets turned into an empty string somewhere along the line. It might be via Jackson conversion (I am using Java and Spring on the backend) or I don't know. But I do know that it has been doing it for years and years and years. I have many calls that return either valid JSON or null if nothing found. Which apparently is now, and again only now with this latest release, being interpreted as an empty string and invalid JSON. For these calls, I would have to tell the api, incorrectly, that I am expecting ```responseType: "text"``` and then convert it myself after checking for an empty string. I can't be alone in this.  :) Can someone give me a valid argument as to why ```responseType: "json"``` should throw an exception if encountering an empty string?
